title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages). S is a scheme and F a locally free O_S-module of rank 2. M = End_{O_S}(F), G = M^* = GL(F), SG = SL(F), PG = PGL(F) = M^*/G_m. A section ρ of M is called 'regular' if it is nowhere scalar on fibres. Equivalently, locally there is a cyclic basis (e0, e1 = ρe0) in which ρ is the companion matrix [[0,-v],[1,w]], with v = det ρ and w = Tr ρ. Equivalently again, the commutant of ρ is A_ρ = O_S + O_S ρ ≅ O_S[x]/(x^2 - wx + v), universally. The next page proves the commutant statement and gives Cor. 1: if ρ is regular, then ρ' is Zariski-locally M^*-conjugate to ρ iff ρ' is regular and det ρ' = det ρ, Tr ρ' = Tr ρ.

This page.
(NB) The conjugation action of G on M, G and SG factors through PG. PG is the fppf quotient of SG by μ_2, and an étale quotient when 2 is invertible. So in the conjugation criteria (6) ρ' = αρα^{-1}, one may assume α ∈ SG, after fppf/étale localization.
(Cor. 2) Let ρ, ξ be sections of G with ρ regular. A local solution α ∈ ΓG of the commutator equation (7) [α,ρ] = ξ, i.e. αρα^{-1} = ξρ, exists iff two conditions hold:
(a) ξρ is regular, i.e. ξ is nowhere on a fibre a scalar multiple of ρ^{-1};
(b) det ξ = 1 and Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ.
The proof applies Cor. 1 to the pair (ρ, ξρ); det(ξρ) = det ρ is equivalent to det ξ = 1.
(Cor. 3) The solutions α form a torsor under the centralizer: α ↦ αt with t ∈ A_ρ^*, i.e. t = cρ + d where det(cρ + d) = c^2 v + wcd + d^2 is invertible (8).

Purpose. This is groundwork for studying 2-dimensional (GL2/SL2) solutions of the 'équation des lacets', i.e. commutator/conjugacy relations among loops in π1 of P^1 minus three points under Galois or GT-type actions. It amounts to a scheme-theoretic analysis of when a given element is a commutator with a fixed regular element.
errors: The parenthetical 'On peut alors prendre α dans SG' and 'OPS α ∈ ΓSG' are not true Zariski-locally. One needs det α to lie in Nm(A_ρ^*)·(squares), which can fail over a field when A_ρ is a non-split quadratic extension. The NB correctly indicates this works only after fppf (étale if 2 is invertible) localization via SG → PG; Cor. 2 itself is stated for Zariski-local α ∈ G.
Minor: 'Cor. 1' is referred to before it appears; it is on the following manuscript page, which suggests the pages were reordered or inserted.
Formula (8) is correct: det(cρ + d) = c^2 χ_ρ(-d/c) = d^2 + wcd + vc^2, with v = det ρ and w = Tr ρ.

ideas.what: Regular sections of End of a rank-2 bundle: nowhere scalar ⇔ locally cyclic (companion-matrix form) ⇔ commutant is O_S + O_S ρ universally
ideas.modern_name: regular elements / regular centralizers of GL_2 over a base scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steinberg, Kostant (fields); SGA3 (Demazure–Grothendieck) for regular elements over schemes
ideas.where_published: SGA3 Exp. XIII–XIV (regular elements in a general setting); the rank-2 explicit form is standard

ideas.what: Conjugacy of regular elements determined by trace and determinant, Zariski-locally (Cor. 1)
ideas.modern_name: Chevalley/Steinberg: regular elements with equal characteristic polynomial are conjugate (Steinberg section)

ideas.what: Criterion for solving [α,ρ] = ξ: ξρ regular, det ξ = 1, Tr ξρ = Tr ρ; solution set a torsor under A_ρ^*
ideas.modern_name: commutator equations in GL_2/SL_2; centralizer torsor; trace (Fricke) conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Fricke–Vogt trace identities; Thompson/Ree on commutators in SL_2)

ideas.what: Reducing conjugation by GL to SL via PGL = SL/μ_2 as an fppf quotient
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2 as fppf quotient of SL_2 by μ_2

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard linear algebra of regular elements of GL_2 over a base scheme, applied to a commutator equation. It is correct up to the Zariski vs fppf localization slip, and is routine groundwork for the GL2-analysis of the loop equations rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Soient ξ, ρ, ξ deux sections de G' should read 'Soient ρ, ξ deux sections de G'.
'trouver loc. 2[?]' is likely 'trouver loc. (Zar)' (cf. 'loc Zar' on the next page).
Condition a) likely reads: 'ξρ est régulier, i.e. ξ n'est multiple scalaire de ρ^{-1} sur aucune fibre'.
The parenthetical after 'quotient fppf de SG' likely reads '(de noyau μ_2, et quotient pour la top. (ét), si 2 inv.)'.
'OPS α ∈ ΓSG(?)' = 'On peut supposer α ∈ Γ SG' (localization understood).
